Playbook.name: Windows — Scheduled Task Created with Suspicious Action - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A scheduled task was created (4698) whose action content contains suspicious patterns - encoded PowerShell, download cradles, or interpreter execution. Triage question: is this a persistence/execution task, or a legitimate scheduled job?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Scheduled tasks are a common persistence and delayed-execution mechanism; an encoded-command task is almost always malicious.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Suspicious scheduled task
Signal.Details: 4698 TaskContent with powershell -enc / frombase64 / download patterns.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host where the task was created.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the scheduled task is malicious persistence/execution or a legitimate job.

Step.name: Task detail: name, action content, creator
Step.Purpose: The task action content reveals the payload (encoded PS, download cradle, LOLBin).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4698" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.TaskName, winlog.event_data.TaskContent | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: TaskContent with -enc/FromBase64String, a download cradle (IEX/DownloadString), or execution from temp/appdata = malicious. A vendor task pointing at a signed binary on a schedule is benign.

Step.name: Was the task created right after a remote/suspicious logon
Step.Purpose: Task persistence created just after remote access links it to an intrusion.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4624","4672") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS c = COUNT(*), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), users = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) BY src | SORT c DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A remote/interactive logon by the creator shortly before the task creation supports an intrusion-driven persistence.

Node.Condition: Task action contains encoded PowerShell/download cradle/temp-path execution.
A verifiable vendor/admin scheduled job under a change record.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SCHTASK-DETAIL, INV-02-SCHTASK-ORIGIN to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the job; close as false_positive.
Delete the task; isolate the host; open IR.
Hunt the creator's other persistence and origin.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A deployment tool creating tasks with wrapper commands.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
